newsitem.title: UK: Siebe boosts H1 profits, more to come.
newsitem.headline: Siebe boosts H1 profits, more to come.

text.p: International engineering group Siebe Plc announced a 32 percent increase in first-half profits on Tuesday and said its strong divisional performances and recent acquisitions meant there was more growth to come.

Taxable profits for the six months to September 30 rose to 190.4 million pounds ($321 million) from 144.2 million a year ago on sales up 22 percent at 1.47 billion. The dividend was increased to 4.9 pence a share from 4.44p on earnings up 25 percent at 24 pence.
"That we performed so well is due to the even spread of our business operations both by geographic region and economic cycle," chairman Barrie Stephens said in his resutls statement.
"Recent quotation and booking activities remain strong, confirmation that Siebe's divisions continue to gain further market shares," he said.
"Add to this the group's successful acquisition programme and you will understand that the board is confident of being able to deliver a further profit increase in the second half."

Siebe bought power controls giant Unitech Plc in April this year which, valued at 520 million pounds, gave the firm its biggest deal since it bought Foxboro, the U.S. process automation controls manufacturer for 357 million pounds in 1990.

Chief executive Allen Yurko said the company had seen strong growth in both its industrial process controls and its temperature and appliance controls businesses, with increased market share making up for any slowdown in market growth.
He said the firm had also pressed ahead with improving its operating performance through cost reductions and restructurings and by improving manufacturing and quality control techniques.
As a result Siebe's group operating margin had been increased to 14.7 percent from 13.8 percent in the last year.
"These are the best Siebe margin improvements in 25 years," he told Reuters in an interview.

Yurko said margins rose to 15.8 percent from 15 percent at the process controls systems division and to 15.5 percent from 14.4 percent at the temperature and appliance controls division, Siebe's two biggest businesses.
"So overall I am upbeat and positive for the second half as well as on into 1997/98," he said.
He said operating profits from existing businesses before acquisitions in the first half of this year were up 17 percent on sales up 8.1 percent.
Productivity at Unitech had been increased 12 percent with the loss of 1,400 jobs and the business was on course to boost earnings this year, Yurko said.

He said Unitech's operating profits were up 10 percent at 21.3 million pounds in the five months since Siebe took over on sales up three percent at 168 million pounds compared to a year ago. There was severe weakness in the semiconductor equipment industry which hit Unitech's Japanese subsidiary Lambda but "even that's starting to turn now," Yurko said.
Unitech and several smaller businesses bought in the six months contributed 176.9 million pounds of sales and 22.6 million in operating profits to the half-year results. ($1=.5936 Pound)
